To: State Legislative Delegation of Hall County, Georgia

From: Town of Clermont, Georgia

WHEREAS, the New Charter for the Town of Clermont, Georgia, known as Georgia Act No. One Thousand and Seventy-Four (1074), is located on pages Four Thousand Seven Hundred and Eighty-Two (4782) through Four Thousand Eight Hundred and Nineteen (4819) of Georgia

Laws, Vol. II, Book II, Replacement Volume; and WHEREAS, said document was signed by the Honorable Zell Miller on the fifth day of

April, 1994; and WHEREAS, the Town of Clermont desires to have said Charter amended so that the procedure for filling vacancies in office is changed to an elective process; and WHEREAS, the Town requests the legislative delegation to introduce the required legislation so that the amendment may be implemented; NOW, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED by the Town of Clermont, Georgia, that:

- 1. Article II, Chapter 2, Section 3-202 of the New Charter shall be deleted.

- 2. The Amended Article III, Chapter 2, Section 3-202 of the New Charter. shall read as follows: "Section 3-202. Filling of vacancies. In the event the office of the mayor or any councilmember shall become vacant by death, removal, disqualification, resignation, or other cause, the remaining members of the council shall temporarily fill the vacancy by appointment from among the citizens of said Town eligible to hold such office under the provisions of this charter. The person so appointed shall only fill the office until such

time as a special election can be held and a person is elected and sworn in to office. Said election shall be held in accordance with this charter and state law concerning the holding of special elections. The person appointed to temporarily fill the office shall be eligible to run in said election." This /Z day of Pe bruang, 19%

To: State Legislative Delegation of Hall County, Georgia

From: Town of Clermont, Georgia

WHEREAS, the New Charter for the Town of Clermont, Georgia, known as Georgia Act No. one thousand and seventy-four (1074), is located on pages four thousand seven hundred and eighty~-two (4782) through four thousand eight hundred and nineteen (4819) of Georgia Laws, Vol. II, Book II, Replacement Volume; and

WHEREAS, said document was signed by the Honorable Zell Miller on the fifth day of April, 1994; and

WHEREAS, it has come to the attention of the Mayor and Councilmembers of the Town of Clermont that the terms of office proscribed by Article III, Chapter 1, Section 3-102, Subsection (b) directly contradict the terms of office as proscribed by the 1992 Charter Amendment (H. B. No. 1728) at Section 1; and

WHEREAS, the terms of office as proscribed by the 1992 Charter Amendment were filled by a vote of the registered voters of Clermont, so that the 1992 Charter Amendment should control this discrepancy in language; and

WHEREAS, the Mayor and Councilmembers desire to clarify this contradiction;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED by the Town of Clermont, Georgia, that:
4:
- 1. Article III, Chapter 1, Section 3-102, Subsection (b) of the

1994 Charter is hereby repealed and deleted in its entirety; 2. A new Article III, Chapter 1, Section 3-102, Subsection (b) is hereby adopted and provides as follows:

"(b) The Mayor and Councilmembers shall be elected from the

Town at large. The Mayor and Councilmembers shall serve terms of four (4) years and until their successors are duly elected and qualified. The three (3) Councilmembers elected at the general municipal election held on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in November of 1995, shall take office at the

first organizational meeting in January, 1996. Thereafter, the officials shall serve a term of four (4) years. The Mayor and two (2) Councilmembers (who were not up for election in 1995) shall serve until their term expires on December 31, 1997. The election for Mayor and the two (2) Councilmembers’ seats shall be held on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in November of 1997. The candidates elected for Mayor and the two (2) Councilmember seats shall take office at the first organizational meeting in January, 1998. Thereafter, the officials shall serve a term of four (4) years. All municipal elections shall be non-partisan, and the names of the candidates shall be listed alphabetically upon the ballot without party label. Candidates for Councilmember seats receiving the highest number of votes shall fill the vacant seats. The candidates seeking the seat of Mayor shall so designate their candidacy. The mayoral candidate receiving a majority of the votes cast shall be declared the winner."
